catalog_entry.label: NBA playoff series cumulative team points (total and spread)
catalog_entry.target: Combined points or cumulative point differential of two teams summed over all games of a playoff series vs a strike
catalog_entry.mechanism: Both contracts sum per-game quantities over a best-of-seven series that stops when one team reaches four wins. The total is approximately series length times a playoff-adjusted per-game total, so its distribution has one mode per possible length (4-7 games) and rungs between modes largely price length. The differential sums game margins; margins also decide who wins each game, so the stopping rule couples them: lopsided series end quickly and accumulate a large differential in few games, while even series run long with margins that partly cancel. A shared matchup regime correlates games, mid-series injuries switch paths, close-out games and blowout truncation shape the decisive margin, and whether overtime counts is not stated in the rules.

inputs.why: Gives per-game win probabilities with home pattern and correlated injuries that drive the stopping rule.
Number of games is the volume of the series total; read as a diagnostic and seed output of the simulator, whose joint draw replaces independent combination.

Per-game expected team points from own pace and efficiency; the unit that is summed.
Possessions per game; the volume per game that compounds over the series.
Points per possession of each offence, lineup-adjusted.

Status vintage at the decision time for the next and later games.
Probability that each star stays healthy across the remaining games of the series.

Matchup pace from both teams' tempo preferences; persists across games of a series.
Expected shooting, turnover, rebounding and FT rates for each side in this matchup.
Scheme profile helps explain adjustments over a series and the scoring regime.
Shooting luck in completed games should be regressed when updating the remaining-games forecast.
Three-point-reliant fast teams have higher per-game variance, widening the summed distribution.
Per-game margin sd scales with pace and total; it sets the spread contract's per-game noise.
Blowout margins shrink after starters sit, capping the cumulative differential.
Benchmark only: its P(OT) is bucketed on the market spread; superseded here by nba.reg_tie_pmf_model and excluded from stages.
Number of OT periods and their scoring, for the rare multi-OT games.
Home-court effect by game under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern.
Altitude and travel only matter for specific venues such as Denver or Utah.
Rest days between games and the layoff before the series change early-game efficiency.
Named crew tendencies apply only to the game whose crew is announced.
Foul drawing and free-throw rate of both teams add points every game.
Wording decides which points count, the strike direction and how incomplete series settle.
Settled outcomes are labels to check simulator calibration across rungs.
Official score corrections are rare at the team-points level.
Aggregation model whose joint law of length, total and differential prices every rung; not a raw information input.
Sets the variance of the summed total and differential, which decides probabilities at rungs away from the centre of each length mode.
Moves the per-game total that is multiplied by series length, and accumulates across games instead of averaging out.
Shapes the per-game total means along each simulated path; margin-by-game-number comes from nba.series_game_conditional_state.
The decisive game is always in the sum, so its margin regime matters disproportionately for the differential contract.
Shifts per-game points for every game of the series and is only partly knowable before each game.
Points and differential already banked in completed games shift every strike for a mid-series decision and can decide the total rung outright.
Overtime game margins are a folded small-margin distribution that sits inside the sum for the spread; used only if OT counts (u1), and supplies the OT-game margin point mass that s3 refers to.

Market-free map from expected margin to each team's points (garbage-time flattening of favourites, late fouling by underdogs); splits the simulated game total into team points for the differential contract.

Market-free blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve; overlaps nba.margin_decay_after_pull, kept as context for P(lead >= 20 entering Q4) rather than a second margin-shrinkage estimate.
Playoff defensive-assignment shift relevant to matchup scoring; the free source is a season-type aggregate and game-level playoff assignments are not shown to be available, so context only.
Executable price path of each rung is needed to evaluate edge and entry, but it is a market price and not a predictor; excluded from every stage and coverage claim.
External sportsbook series total or spread lines are an independent market estimate of the same distribution; benchmark for comparing simulator output, never a model input.
Rung monotonicity across strikes is needed to check that simulated P(total >= K) is non-increasing and to evaluate rung pairs; derived from prices, so it is a benchmark and evaluation check only.
Reliability by price bucket is a market-family calibration diagnostic computed from prices and outcomes, not a pregame input to the score distribution.
Market-free regulation-tie probability per game from the own-model margin density; sets OT incidence that adds a period of points if OT counts (u1).

interactions.hypothesis: Series total is length times per-game total, so sensitivity of a rung to the per-game total is highest near a length mode and lower, though not zero, between modes.
The stopping rule couples per-game margins and series length, so expected cumulative differential grows concavely with the rating gap.
A mid-series star absence switches the path regime, moving margins, win probability and series length together.
Playoff pace and whistle shifts apply to every game and add to the shared series factor, so they move the whole total distribution rather than averaging out.

contract.settlement_definition: Total: YES if the two teams 'collectively score at least' the strike (sampled strike 900) over the series; the sampled strike is an integer, so at-least K is exact with no tie. Spread: YES if the named team scores 'more than' the strike (sampled strike 9.5, floor_strike 9.5, strike_type greater_or_equal) more points than the opponent, summed as 'cumulative points scored throughout the series'; with integer game scores a half-point strike cannot tie, but only the 9.5 strike was observed so this is not verified for other strikes. Both sum every game actually played until the series ends. Rules do not state whether overtime points count (assumed included in official final scores), what happens if a game or the series is not completed, or the source of truth; these are open.

rules_evidence.quote: collectively score at least 900 points, then the market resolves to Yes
rules_evidence.establishes: Total contract is an at-least (>=) threshold on the combined points of both teams over the series.

rules_evidence.quote: If San Antonio scores more than 9.5 more points than New York in the 2026 Pro Basketball Finals
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread contract is oriented on a named team with a strike on the cumulative differential; the sampled 9.5 strike cannot tie with integer scores, other strikes were not observed.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on cumulative points scored throughout the series.
rules_evidence.establishes: The differential is summed over all games of the series, not a single game, but OT inclusion and source are not stated.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime: neither series' rules mention overtime; official game scores include OT, but explicit inclusion is unverified and matters for rungs near a mode.
Early determination: a total of at-least K is decided as soon as the running sum crosses K, before the series ends; whether Kalshi settles early or waits for the series end is not stated.
Orientation: the spread is written for one named team; whether mirror markets for the other team or negative strikes exist is not visible from one sample.
Only Finals series were sampled (NYK vs SAS 2026); earlier-round series may use different strikes, team naming or wording.
Incomplete series (cancelled or forfeited game, suspended play) has no stated treatment.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; assumed official NBA final box scores (NBA.com) summed over all series games, OT inclusion unconfirmed.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is a random sum over a random number of games. Per game, possessions (slower in the playoffs and matchup-specific) times points per possession (opponent-adjusted, lineup-dependent, partly shooting luck, plus a playoff whistle that cuts free throws) give each team's points; their sum is the game total and their difference the margin. The margin decides the game winner, and the series stops at four wins under a 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern, so the number of summed games is endogenous. For the total, length dominates: each game adds roughly a full game's combined points, so the distribution is a mixture with one mode per length and strikes between modes mainly price length. For the differential, the stopping rule couples margin size with length: a dominant team piles up margin but over fewer games, while a balanced series lasts longer with cancelling margins; the decisive game is always included and blowout truncation and close-out effort shape it. A shared matchup factor makes games correlated, in-series adjustments drift totals by game number, mid-series injuries switch the regime, and overtime adds a discrete jump if it counts.

stages.name: Series-start strength and availability paths
stages.description: Before game 1 each team's strength is the rating of the players who will actually play over the next two weeks, not the regular-season average. Rotations shorten and stars play more minutes; an injury report vintage fixes the next game's scenario, and a per-game health hazard spreads probability over availability paths for later games, where a star loss mid-series is the largest regime change for both margins and length.
stages.distribution: Discrete mixture over availability paths; each path has a nearly deterministic rating shift, so the mixture is lumpy rather than normal.

stages.name: Per-game possessions and efficiency in the playoff matchup
stages.description: Each game's points per team come from matchup pace (both tempo preferences, slowed by a round-specific playoff shift) times points per possession against this defence, including free throws under a playoff whistle that allows more contact. Venue alternates under 2-2-1-1-1, rest varies from one to three days, and coaches adjust coverages after each game, so totals tend to drift by game number.
stages.distribution: Game total roughly normal with sd near 18-20 points; per-team points slightly right-skewed by three-point variance and overtime.

stages.name: Per-game margin, win and truncation
stages.description: The margin of each game decides its winner and is what the spread contract sums. Its sd scales with pace and total; big leads shrink after starters are pulled, overtime games end within a few points, and close-out and elimination games have their own effort and blowout profile, with a bounce-back tendency for the team that lost the previous game.
stages.distribution: Margin roughly normal around the rating gap plus home edge, with compressed far tails from garbage time and a point mass of small margins from OT games.

stages.name: Stopping rule and series length
stages.description: Game winners accumulate until one side has four wins, so the count of summed games is 4 to 7 and depends on per-game win probabilities, home pattern and dependence between games. Length is the main volume of the total contract and sets how many margins enter the differential; the higher seed's extra home games in games 5 and 7 matter only in long paths. The length pmf is an output of the joint simulator (nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator), with nba.series_length_distribution kept as a cross-check.
stages.distribution: Discrete on {4,5,6,7}; game-to-game correlation and adjustments make sweeps and seven-game series both differ from an independent binomial.

stages.name: Aggregation into series total and cumulative differential
stages.description: The simulator sums game totals and margins along each path. Because a shared matchup factor persists across games, the sum's sd exceeds sqrt(N) times the single-game sd. The total becomes a mixture with modes near N times the per-game total; the differential is coupled to length through the stopping rule, so lopsided paths are short with large sums and even paths are long with cancelling margins.
stages.distribution: Total: mixture over N in {4..7} with modes about one per-game total (~215-225 points) apart and within-mode sd of roughly 40-65 points, so troughs between modes stay well above zero density; differential: sign follows the series winner, so it is bimodal (a lump on each side of 0) for near-even matchups and unimodal only for lopsided ones, with length-dependent variance.

stages.name: Settlement against the rung
stages.description: The running sums are compared to the strike at the series end: at-least K for the total, more-than S for the named team's differential. The total can be decided before the series ends once the sum crosses K. Rules state cumulative points throughout the series but not overtime treatment, incomplete-series handling or the source of truth, so those branches carry contract risk. Mid-series, the banked points of completed games (nba.series_banked_points_state) shift each strike and can decide the total before the series ends.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the official scores; ambiguity is concentrated in OT inclusion near rungs and in rare incomplete-series branches.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency of the active playoff set.

opponent_matchup.note: Same opponent every game, so matchup effects repeat and feed the shared factor.

availability_news.note: Next-game status plus per-game health hazard over the series horizon.

environment.note: Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1; altitude for specific venues.

game_context_script.note: Garbage time, close-out games, overtime and the banked score state that anchors a mid-series decision.

pace_volume.note: Games in the series (length pmf generated jointly by the simulator) and possessions per game are both volume.

efficiency_conversion.note: Points per possession with luck separated.

distribution_variance.note: Mixture over length, within-series correlation, per-game sd.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Series score, rest between games, elimination stakes.

settlement_contract.note: OT inclusion, early determination and source are open (see unresolved); banked points convert the strike into a remaining-games requirement.

nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.label: Game-by-game series simulator for the joint law of series length, cumulative total and cumulative point differential
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.mechanism: Draws each game's (home points, away points) jointly, records the winner, stops when one side reaches four wins, and sums points and margins over the realised games, so length and points are generated by one process rather than combined independently.
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.rationale: This is an aggregation model, not a raw information input: it is listed because every rung is a tail probability of its output and the catalog needs its definition. The series total is a random sum over a random number of games, and the number of games depends on the same per-game margins that the spread contract sums. Multiplying an expected length by an expected per-game total loses the multimodal shape (one mode per possible length) and the negative coupling between lopsided margins and short series, which is exactly where rung probabilities live.
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.measurement: Monte Carlo (>=200k paths) over the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern from the current series state; per game draw team points from a bivariate distribution with means from own-model pace x points per possession for that game's venue, rest and projected lineups, a series-level random effect shared across games, and a correlation between total and |margin| fitted on 2004+ playoff games; output P(N=k), P(total>=K) and P(diff>=S) for every listed rung, recomputed at each as-of timestamp.
free_sources: Derived from Basketball-Reference / NBA Stats playoff box scores and own-model ratings
raw_data: playoff game box scores (team points by period incl. OT, home team, series id and game number)
own-model expected possessions and points per possession
nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator.why: Every rung of both series contracts is a tail probability of this joint distribution; it is the core aggregation step.

nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.label: Series-level shared TOTAL (scoring-environment) random effect and its covariance with margin residuals
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.mechanism: Two teams meeting four to seven times in two weeks share a scoring environment (tempo, scheme, shooting conditions) that persists across games, so game totals inside a series are positively correlated beyond pre-series ratings; this input owns the total-side dependence and the total-margin covariance only.
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.rationale: If games were independent, the sd of a five-game series total would be about sqrt(5) times the single-game sd; a positive intraclass correlation inflates that, fattening both tails of the series total and shifting probability toward far rungs. The margin-side series random effect (sd about 2 points), the previous-game margin and the elimination dummy are already defined in nba.series_game_conditional_state and are consumed from it, not re-estimated here. The size of this effect is small-sample and must be estimated with shrinkage.
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.measurement: Fit a random-effects model on playoff games 2004-present: residual of GAME TOTAL versus the pre-series own-model expectation, with a series random intercept; report the intraclass correlation and its posterior sd, shrunk toward a regular-season back-to-back-matchup estimate; update the series effect after each completed game with a normal-normal conjugate step. Also estimate the covariance between the total residual and the margin residual within game; the margin random effect itself is taken from nba.series_game_conditional_state so that the simulator holds a single fitted margin-dependence parameter.
raw_data: playoff game totals with series id and game number
nba.series_shared_scoring_factor.why: Sets the variance of the summed total, which decides probabilities at rungs away from the centre of each length mode, and supplies the total-margin covariance the differential needs.

nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.label: Playoff-versus-regular-season pace and efficiency shift by round
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.mechanism: Playoff games are played slower, with tighter rotations of better players, more half-court sets and more physical defence, so possessions and points per possession differ from the same teams' regular-season rates, and the shift grows by round.
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.rationale: Regular-season ratings applied directly overstate playoff possessions; summing the bias over four to seven games makes it a material miss on a series total ladder whose rungs are spaced a few tens of points apart. The shift is also matchup-dependent: fast teams lose more pace than slow ones.
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.measurement: For each playoff game since 2004, compute actual possessions and offensive rating minus the regular-season opponent-adjusted expectation for that pairing; pool by round with a hierarchical model (round level, team-tempo slope); report mean shift in possessions per 48 and points per 100 with sd, using a 6-season half-life to track era changes.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference / NBA Stats team game logs (regular season and playoffs)
raw_data: team game logs with possessions, points, opponent (regular season and playoffs, 2004-present)
regular-season opponent-adjusted team ratings and pace
nba.playoff_round_scoring_shift.why: Moves the per-game total that is multiplied by series length, and accumulates across games instead of averaging out.

nba.series_game_number_drift.label: Within-series drift of game TOTALS by game number (adjustments and familiarity)
nba.series_game_number_drift.mechanism: Coaches adjust coverages and rotations after each game and players learn the matchup, so later games in a series tend to be scored differently from game 1 (total-side fixed effects by game number 1-7); margin-side game-number, previous-game bounce-back and rest effects are owned by nba.series_game_conditional_state (its 'games played' and previous-margin features) and only consumed here.
nba.series_game_number_drift.rationale: Late games (5-7) exist only in longer series, so a drift by game number changes the per-game total exactly in the paths that cross high rungs, ; the margin level by game number is not re-fitted here because nba.series_game_conditional_state already carries games played as a margin feature and home margin by game number is confounded with the 2-2-1-1-1 venue alternation.
nba.series_game_number_drift.measurement: From playoff games 2004+: regress GAME TOTAL residual (vs pre-game own-model total) on game-number fixed effects 1-7 with series random effects, after partialling out rest days using the coefficients from nba.series_game_conditional_state (not re-fitted here); margins are not modelled here (margin by games played comes from nba.series_game_conditional_state); shrink game 6-7 coefficients toward game 5 because of sparse counts; output per-game total mean adjustments used by the simulator.
raw_data: playoff game totals by game number and series
rest days as defined in nba.series_game_conditional_state
nba.series_game_number_drift.why: Shapes the per-game total means along each simulated path rather than using one per-game total for the whole series.

nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.label: Margin spread, blowout and starter-truncation profile in close-out and elimination games
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.mechanism: When one team can clinch or is facing elimination, effort and rotation decisions change the SPREAD of margins and the blowout and garbage-time profile (a team down 0-3 may concede late; game-7 margins are compressed); the mean shift for elimination games is the dummy in nba.series_game_conditional_state and is not re-estimated here.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.rationale: The final game of every series is a close-out game, so its margin enters every cumulative differential; if close-out games are more lopsided (or, for game 7s, tighter) than ratings imply, the differential's tails move. Effects are asymmetric by which side is on the brink.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.measurement: From playoff play-by-play 2004+: classify each game by state (clinch opportunity for home/away, elimination for both, neither); fit margin sd, blowout (>=20) probability and starter minutes after a 20-point lead by state, controlling for rating gap and venue, taking the mean elimination shift from nba.series_game_conditional_state; shrink state effects toward the neutral-game values with a prior sd of 2 points on sd-ratio terms.
raw_data: Playoff play-by-play with score and substitutions 2004+
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.why: The decisive game is always in the sum, so the width and truncation of its margin matter disproportionately for the differential contract.

nba.playoff_whistle_regime.label: Round-level playoff foul and free-throw environment with unknown future crews
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.mechanism: Playoff officiating tolerates more contact, cutting fouls and free-throw attempts relative to the regular season; crews are assigned game by game and announced on the morning of each game, so for later games only the round-level pool distribution is knowable.
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.rationale: Free throws are a large share of points and also add stoppages that change late-game possessions; a series-long shift of a few attempts per game sums to a material number of points. Using a single named crew for the whole series would be wrong because each game draws a different crew.
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.measurement: Per playoff game since 2010: personal fouls and FTA per 100 possessions minus each team pair's regular-season rate; model by round with crew random effects; for unplayed games integrate over the round's officials pool (empirical frequency of crew chiefs assigned in that round) and use the announced crew only for the game whose assignment is out.
raw_data: referee assignments per playoff game with announcement time
team PF and FTA per game
nba.playoff_whistle_regime.why: Shifts per-game points for every game of the series and is only partly knowable before each game.

nba.series_banked_points_state.label: Points already banked in completed series games (running team totals, running combined total and running differential)
nba.series_banked_points_state.mechanism: Both contracts sum over every game of the series, so once k games are final the sum splits into a known banked part and an unplayed remainder; the decision-time probability is a tail probability of the remainder measured from the shifted strike, not from the full strike.
nba.series_banked_points_state.rationale: For any decision after game 1 the banked sum is the largest single determinant of both contracts: a 900 total rung after three games with about 650 banked needs only about 250 more points, which is a length question (one more game or two), and the rung can already be decided (YES with certainty) once the banked sum reaches the strike. For the spread, a banked differential of +30 turns a 9.5 strike into a bet that the opponent outscores the leader by less than the remaining cushion. Using a series-start distribution after games are played would ignore this realised state.
nba.series_banked_points_state.measurement: As of timestamp T (decision time), take every series game with a final official box score published before T: for each, team points including overtime. Compute B_total = sum over completed games of (home pts + away pts); D_team = sum of (named team pts - opponent pts). Rung conversion: remaining requirement for the total is K_rem = K - B_total (P=1 if K_rem <= 0, otherwise tail probability of the remaining-games total under nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator started from the current series score); for the spread S_rem = S - D_team on the remaining-games differential. Games in progress at T contribute nothing unless the decision uses a live-score feed (excluded here); a game with a pending or corrected score is flagged and re-read after the correction window; units are points, no shrinkage because the quantity is realised.
free_sources: Basketball-Reference playoff box scores / line scores
NBA Stats leaguegamelog (final team points per game)
raw_data: final team points by game for completed series games incl. OT with game end timestamp
current series score and next scheduled game and venue
nba.series_banked_points_state.why: Realised banked totals and differential are the starting state for every rung once the series is under way, and they decide the total outright when the banked sum passes the strike.

nba.series_model.reason: Supplies per-game win probabilities and the home pattern, but it outputs series win and length only, not points; the stopping simulator extends it to sums, so it is an upstream component rather than the main input. Scope split: owns the per-game win probabilities and home pattern only; the dependence parameter is taken from nba.series_game_conditional_state rather than fitted again.

nba.series_length_distribution.reason: Series length is the dominant driver of the total, but in this archetype it is an output of nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator (length generated jointly with points) and not an independent primary input; the dynamic-programme length pmf is kept as a cross-check and as seed for per-game win probabilities, and the simulated P(N) is what prices rungs. Using it as a separately combined primary factor would reintroduce independence between length and margins.

nba.series_game_conditional_state.reason: Needed to condition each simulated game on series score, rest days and injuries accrued so far; it also re-prices the remaining sum once some games are played. Secondary because its effect is on game-level means already in the simulator. Scope split: sole owner of the margin-level dependence (series random effect, previous-game margin, games played, elimination dummy); nba.series_shared_scoring_factor, nba.series_game_number_drift and nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile consume these parameters and add only total-side dependence, total-side game-number effects and truncation spread.

nba.own_model_team_totals.reason: The per-game expected team points are the summand of the total contract and, as a difference, of the spread contract; it is market-free by construction, which is required here, and must be re-evaluated per venue and lineup.

nba.pace.reason: Possessions scale every game's total, but the regular-season figure must be passed through the playoff round shift; as a raw input it is a component of the own-model team total rather than an independent driver.

nba.off_rtg.reason: Offensive efficiency against the specific opponent sets per-game points and, for the spread, each side's share; secondary because it enters via the own-model team totals and needs playoff-rotation re-weighting.

nba.def_rtg.reason: Defensive rating is the mirror of off_rtg in the per-game total and margin; a portion is opponent shooting luck, so it should be regressed before being summed over several games in a series.

nba.lineup_adj_rating.reason: Ratings for the active set matter more here than in a single game because an absence lasting several games shifts margin, win probability and length together; this input carries that availability effect into each game.

nba.injuries_pit.reason: The decision-time injury report decides the scenario for the next game and seeds the hazard for later ones; a star ruled out mid-series is the largest single source of path change for both contracts.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.reason: Turns a point-in-time status into a per-game availability path over up to two weeks; built for round-reach contracts but directly reusable for the remaining-games horizon of a series sum.

nba.playoff_rotation.reason: Playoff rotations shorten and stars play more minutes, which changes the lineups whose ratings feed each game; it overlaps partly with the round scoring shift but is player-level rather than league-level.

nba.joint_pace_interaction.reason: The two teams' tempo preferences combine into a matchup pace that repeats every game of the series, making it a source of the shared series factor rather than independent per-game noise.

nba.four_factors_matchup.reason: Explains how the margin and total arise in this specific pairing (for example, glass versus turnover battles); useful for per-game means but largely captured once off_rtg and def_rtg are opponent-adjusted.

nba.def_scheme.reason: Scheme labels (drop, switch, zone) help interpret game-number drift and adjustment effects but are coarse and partly hidden; context rather than a direct numeric driver of summed points.

nba.three_pt_luck.reason: After early games a hot or cold three-point run moves both the total and the differential; most of it is noise, so separating luck from shot quality keeps in-series updates from overreacting.

nba.team_points_variance_by_style.reason: Per-game variance of each team's points feeds the width of every length mode; style-based variance matters most for rungs away from mode centres where probability is sensitive to sd.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.reason: The spread contract sums margins, so their sd per game matters directly, and it is defined on own-model pace and total rather than a line, which keeps it market-free.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.reason: Lopsided games contribute less margin than ratings imply once benches play; for a cumulative differential the cap on large margins limits how fast a dominant team accumulates points.

nba.ot_model.reason: Its catalog measurement is 'Empirical P(OT) by |spread| bucket', i.e. P(OT) conditioned on the market point spread, so it is market-derived; the market-free nba.reg_tie_pmf_model (P(OT) from the own-model margin density at zero) replaces it in s3 and coverage, with OT points from nba.ot_period_distribution.

nba.ot_period_distribution.reason: Multiple overtimes are rare but add large jumps to one game's total; mainly context for tail rungs, and it only matters if OT is counted in cumulative points.

nba.venue.reason: Home-court advantage flips by game under the 2-2-1-1-1 pattern, so the higher seed's extra home game in games 5 and 7 tilts both who wins those games and the margin accumulated in long series.

nba.travel_altitude.reason: Travel in a series is between the same two cities with rest days between games, so its effect is small; altitude matters only when Denver or Utah host, making this a weak, venue-specific adjustment.

nba.rest_travel.reason: Playoff games are separated by one to three days and a team may arrive after a long layoff or straight from a game 7; the effect on points is modest but differs between the two teams early in a series.

nba.referee_crew.reason: Crew foul tendencies shift free throws for one game, but crews are assigned per game and announced on game day, so for the series sum only the next game's crew is known; the round-level regime carries the rest.

nba.fouls_ft.reason: Free-throw volume is a stable team trait that adds points in every game of the series and also lengthens close games; it complements the playoff whistle regime, which shifts the league-wide level.

m.rules_text.reason: The rules say cumulative points throughout the series but not whether overtime counts or how a cancelled game is treated, so the versioned text is required to know the target being predicted.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Settled series outcomes are the labels for checking the joint length-and-points calibration; there are only about fifteen series per season, so they are context for validation, not a predictor.

nba.stat_corrections.reason: Team points are rarely corrected after a game, unlike player assists or rebounds, so corrections are unlikely to move a summed series total; kept only as a weak check on the settlement source.

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.reason: Overtime game margins are a folded small-margin distribution that sits inside the sum for the spread; used only if OT counts (u1), and supplies the OT-game margin point mass that s3 refers to. Not duplicated by a new input in this record.

nba.team_points_margin_curve.reason: Market-free map from expected margin to each team's points (garbage-time flattening of favourites, late fouling by underdogs); splits the simulated game total into team points for the differential contract. Not duplicated by a new input in this record.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.reason: Market-free blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve; overlaps nba.margin_decay_after_pull, kept as context for P(lead >= 20 entering Q4) rather than a second margin-shrinkage estimate.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.reason: Playoff defensive-assignment shift relevant to matchup scoring; the free source is a season-type aggregate and game-level playoff assignments are not shown to be available, so context only.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is a benchmark: it measures what the market believes about the same rung and is never fed to the simulator.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook series lines are market-derived prices; used only to compare against the market-free simulator.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-strike implied distribution comes from prices; used as a consistency check on the simulator.

nba.market_calibration_bias.reason: Calibration by price bucket is market-derived and applies after model probabilities exist.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.reason: Market-free P(OT) per game from the own-model margin density at zero with an empirical excess factor ('use own-model mu, not closing lines'); replaces nba.ot_model's spread-bucketed rate and matters only if OT points count (u1).

interactions.mechanism: Within the simulator the series total is about simulated length times per-game total (length drawn jointly, not from the separate DP pmf), so a 5-point shift in per-game total moves a 4-game sum by 20 and a 7-game sum by 35; a rung at a mode centre is highly sensitive to per-game total while a rung in a trough is less sensitive, by an amount that depends on the within-mode sd (about 40-65 points).
interactions.how_to_test: On historical series compare the realised total minus N times pre-series per-game expectation across N; compute the rung-probability derivative with respect to per-game total by rung position.

interactions.mechanism: Margins decide game wins, so large positive margins for one side shorten the series; the cumulative differential and length are negatively dependent, and treating them as independent overstates the differential in lopsided matchups and understates its spread in even ones.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress cumulative differential on series length and pre-series rating gap in 2004+ series; compare simulator output with and without coupling of margin and winner.

interactions.mechanism: Losing a star mid-series shifts every remaining game's margin by several points and the win probability with it; this can lengthen a series the injured team was winning or shorten one it was losing, moving total and differential at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare series in which a top-two player missed games after game 1 with matched series without, on realised length and differential relative to pre-series projection.

interactions.mechanism: The decisive game's margin regime depends on series state: a team trailing 0-3 may concede late and lose big, while game-7 margins compress; because the decisive game always counts, this changes differential tails asymmetrically.
interactions.how_to_test: Margin mean and sd in close-out games by series state (3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3) versus non-close-out games, controlling for rating gap and venue.

interactions.mechanism: Fewer possessions and fewer free throws per possession multiply into lower per-game points, and since both apply to every game they add to the series-level factor, shifting the whole total mixture down rather than averaging out across games.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose playoff total residuals into possessions and FTA per possession shifts by round; check whether the series random effect shrinks once both are included.

interactions.mechanism: Large leads shrink once starters sit, so each game's contribution to a dominant team's differential saturates; combined with fewer games in lopsided series, the cumulative differential grows much slower than the rating gap at the top end.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot per-game realised margin against pre-game expected margin in playoff games and fit a saturating curve; compare simulated differential with linear versus saturated margins.

interactions.mechanism: Once banked points approach the strike, the rung reduces to whether one more or two more games are played, so probability switches from a smooth tail to a length bet; when the banked sum already exceeds the strike the total is certain, a hard threshold in the remaining requirement K - B.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate rung probabilities after games 1-5 of historical series with and without conditioning on banked points; compare calibration for rungs whose remaining requirement K-B lies within one game total of zero.

nonlinearities.shape: soft staircase in the strike of the simulated P(total >= K): steep near length-mode centres, shallower but non-flat between modes
nonlinearities.why: Each extra game adds roughly a full game of points, so P(total >= K) falls in steps near 4x, 5x, 6x and 7x the per-game total; with single-game sd about 18-20, a positive shared factor and mean uncertainty multiplied by N, within-mode sd is roughly 40-65 points against a mode spacing of about 220, so troughs keep a sizeable fraction of peak density. The step sharpness depends on the fitted shared-factor size (u4).

nonlinearities.shape: concave expected differential in the per-game rating gap
nonlinearities.why: A larger rating gap increases each game's margin but shortens the series, so fewer margins are summed; expected cumulative differential rises sub-linearly and its variance falls as the gap grows.

nonlinearities.shape: discrete jump of one extra period of combined points
nonlinearities.why: An overtime game adds a five-minute period of points to one game's total, so rung probabilities near a mode edge jump with the market-free regulation-tie probability (P(OT)) if overtime is counted in cumulative points.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at K - banked total <= 0 (probability 1), steep within one game total of that point
nonlinearities.why: The total contract cannot go back once the running sum has crossed the strike, and just below it a single additional game decides, so response to the banked sum is a kink then a step in series length, not linear.

required_data.timestamp_requirement: Final box score values as of game end; seasons strictly before the decision season for fitted parameters. For banked points, only games with a final score published before the decision time T; a correction window is applied before a score is treated as settled.
